mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to higher S&P 500 forward 5-day returns as the cost of capital decreases.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (25th percentile), or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.5% (UNRATE) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that suppress consumer spending and corporate profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust aggregate demand, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST are above their 3-month moving averages, or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A negative month-over-month change in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns during supply shock regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO growth is negative, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) reflects robust consumer demand for residential construction, boosting related industries and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annualized inflation rate above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL) prompts Federal Reserve tightening, increasing real interest rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decrease in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates severe labor market contraction, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, driving negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or Rank IC for interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly real GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates strong economic expansion, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth is above 2.0% (75th percentile), or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
